statement: For every integer ell>=1, every integer n>=1, and every real weighted tournament matrix A in [0,1]^(n by n) with A+A^T=J (hence A_ii=1/2), let H_ell be the oriented cycle on 4ell cyclic vertices with clockwise edge word (++--) repeated ell times, and define t_Hell(A) by summing weights over all vertex maps and dividing by n^(4ell). Then t_Hell(A)>=16^(-ell), so the ENTIRE 2-subdivided alternating-even-cycle family in immutable source.md Problem3.23 is LTS, with no restriction on the spectral perturbation. More precisely, for B=(A-J/2)/n and E=t_Hell(A)-16^(-ell), E>=16^(-ell)||B||op^(4ell); equality in the density bound holds exactly at A=J/2. For each fixed ell, exponent4ell cannot be decreased in any positive-constant bound of this form over all weighted tournaments. The proof rests on ||(uu^T/2+B)^2||op>=1/4 for arbitrary real unit u and real skew B, established by exact identity(R).
contribution: Proposed complete resolution of the original explicitly posed all-length local question, strengthened to a global weighted inequality and a dimension-free forcing modulus with optimal exponent. The standard almost-skew block reduction is credited to prior work; the proposed substantive step is a square-norm Rayleigh certificate and second-eigenvalue control that bypass the verified earlier short-cycle criterion and inapplicable directed-edge transfer. No equivalent full-family implication was found in the inspected current primary sources. Correctness, current novelty and theoretical significance remain subject to actual fresh review; the dossier identifies incomplete old operator leads and does not assert priority or acceptance.
